tags.gist: Summarizes its positions: backs the competency-based framework and asks FDA to put regulatory clarity and least-burdensome principles first.
Strongly supports FDA's collaborative approach and calls the competency-based framework sound and genuinely innovative.
Asks FDA to pair the framework with a published pathway decision matrix, CMS coordination and a GenAI presubmission mechanism favoring small sponsors.
Endorses evaluating devices against defined competencies, likening it to how a cardiologist's expertise is validated across scenarios.
Wants international harmonization treated as a first-order priority, at minimum mutual recognition of benchmarking evidence across jurisdictions.
Wants a published decision matrix linking each risk tier to its regulatory pathway and premarket evidence requirements.
Strongly supports the two-axis framework as the right organizing principle for GenAI risk stratification.
Wants third-party model dependency added as an explicit risk dimension, with opaque externally controlled models raising baseline risk.
Wants reversibility treated as a separate first-order risk dimension, since the consequence axis does not fully capture irreversibility.
Wants temporal urgency, real-time versus asynchronous use, added as a risk distinction the framework currently lacks.
Supports a directiveness spectrum but wants a rebuttable presumption that outputs with specific numeric parameters are action-directing.
Supports treating patient-facing and clinician-facing applications differently because patients lack training to contextualize outputs.
Wants clear boundaries so general patient information tools are not treated as action-directing, unlike tools giving specific clinical recommendations.
Wants manufacturers to specify the intended user's competency level and validate performance within that user population.
Wants risk assessed at the interaction level, with the highest-risk plausible turn setting classification and conversations constrained to a defined envelope.
Wants asymmetric standards weighting under-escalation more heavily, while not dismissing over-escalation in resource-constrained settings.
Calls the competency-based approach appropriate because it mirrors board certification and credentialing of human clinicians.
Wants FDA to publish, before finalizing, a matrix mapping risk tier to 510(k), De Novo or PMA and evidence requirements, with examples.
Calls the benchmarking architecture sound but wants required specialty domain modules developed with professional societies.
Says contamination of public benchmarks is documented, so good scores may hide clinical failures that could harm patients.
Wants a sequestered national benchmark repository with blinded third-party scoring, and third-party validation of sponsor benchmarks.
Wants prospective trials reserved for autonomous patient-facing Class III devices, with shadow deployment sufficing for supervised Class II devices.
Warns that synthetic data from similar model families yields circular validation that hides the device's real failure modes.
Wants out-of-distribution validation required when synthetic data is used, and real-world data as the primary evidence for subgroups.
Rejects the median practicing clinician as primary comparator for specialty devices, since it would normalize prevailing suboptimal care.
Wants board-certified specialist performance as the comparator for specialty devices, codified in guidance.
Finds delayed specialist review an appropriate comparator for devices expanding access in underserved settings, and wants it codified.
Supports third-party testing but wants ASCA expanded to AI benchmarking bodies with published fees, avoiding a testing duopoly.
Wants each modality benchmarked separately plus proof the integrated device is not degraded, with companion multimodal guidance.
Finds accepting more premarket uncertainty for stronger postmarket monitoring sound and necessary given probabilistic, drifting performance.
Conditions the trade on a fully prespecified, enforceable monitoring plan with metrics, cadence, triggers and action thresholds.
Proposes a default risk-tiered cadence: quarterly, semi-annual or annual review with corresponding reporting to FDA.
Lists triggers for out-of-cycle reassessment, such as foundation model changes, adverse event clusters and peer regulator actions.
Finds supervisory agents promising but wants performance standards, periodic evaluation of the agent and mandatory human review of alerts.
Wants each stakeholder class's monitoring duties codified, with manufacturers keeping primary reporting and remediation obligations.
Says PCCPs need substantial adaptation because prompt, retrieval and guardrail changes differ from firmware updates.
Proposes three change categories: locked elements needing new submissions, PCCP-eligible supervised elements, and documentation-only monitored elements.
Wants explicit example lists for each change category, updated annually as development practices evolve.
Wants authorization conditioned on contractual rights to at least ninety days of notice before material foundation model changes.
Wants version pins with validation gates, a ban on unvalidated automatic updates, and more premarket evidence where notice rights are unavailable.
Says voluntary master files will fail because developers have incentives to withhold, leaving only transparent actors participating.
Proposes a higher premarket evidence burden for devices whose foundation model lacks an adequate master file, as a filing incentive.
Lists minimum master file contents, including data provenance, known failure modes, subgroup benchmarks, version history and update notification protocol.
Says the framework's advisory-device concepts are insufficient for agentic systems, with the highest stakes in implantable closed-loop devices.
Wants mandatory human confirmation before any irreversible agentic action, redefining oversight as pre-action authorization.
Proposes a risk-calibrated action budget capping consecutive autonomous actions before a human checkpoint.
Wants a validated fail-safe mode, defined premarket, for when an agentic device loses supervisory connectivity.
Wants a separate working group on agentic AI in surgical robotics, given irreversibility and time pressure.
Wants a small business pathway with fee relief, GenAI-experienced presubmission reviewers, modular submissions and shared anonymized feedback.
Urges urgent harmonization with the EU, Health Canada, TGA and IMDRF, starting with each accepting the others' benchmarking evidence.
Commends the paper, calling the competency-based framework and two-axis risk assessment the right structures.
Urges three commitments: a pathway decision matrix, FDA-CMS coordination, and a GenAI presubmission program supporting small manufacturers.
Says the framework will shape medical AI for a generation and trusts FDA to get it right with least-burdensome principles.
